newsitem.title: ROMANIA: NEW ROMANIAN COMMERCIAL BANK GETS LICENCE - CENTRAL BANK.
newsitem.headline: NEW ROMANIAN COMMERCIAL BANK GETS LICENCE - CENTRAL BANK.

text.p: Romania's central bank said it had awarded a banking operation licence to Banca Comerciala Astra SA, based in the Transylvanian city of Brasov.
Astra has a subcribed share capital of 12 billion lei, of which 98 percent is held by private companies and individuals. It is expected to launch its first operations by December.

Earlier this year the central bank raised the minimum capital requirements for a banking licence to 25 billion lei from 12 billion and said all operational commercial banks must reach that level by end-1998.
Romania has 30 fully-licensed banks of which six are state-run. It also has eight branches of foreign-banks.

Three weeks ago Romania's upper house of Senate approved a long-awaited bill on bank privatisation, a key requirement under loan accords with international lenders. The bill has yet to pass parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
